title: Normalized presentations of derived coefficient extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small category, $J$ a Grothendieck topology, and $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ the category of modules over each commutative ring sheaf $R$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_a$ for restriction along $a:R\to S$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $E_a$ for the ordinary sheafified scalar extension with its sectionwise pure tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A scalar-extension presentation consists of an additive functor with exactly the objects and maps of $E_a$, a functor $L_a:D(R)\to D(S)$, and a universal left-derived counit $Q_hL_a\to E_{a,h}Q_h$ [def-sfb-left-derived-functor]. The pure section in a presented extension is transported by its object equality. Given presentations $p_a$ for every ring map, normalized successive-extension data consist of ordinary isomorphisms $E_aE_b\cong E_{ab}$ sending $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $b(s)t\otimes x$ with inverse $t\otimes x\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes x)$, derived isomorphisms $L_aL_b\cong L_{ab}$, and their computation equations through the universal counits on every flat-term K-flat complex [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The counit for $a$, and the counit for $b$ on the extension along $a$, are invertible on these complexes. The data also include ordinary extension-restriction adjunctions with unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, exact derived restrictions with their homotopy-localization factorizations, derived adjunctions with the corresponding unit equation on K-flat representatives, ordinary and derived restriction compositors normalized by the identity on underlying sections and their localization equation, the composite-unit equation, associativity of three successive extensions, and naturality in commuting coefficient squares. The comparison for a commuting square $a\beta=\alpha a'$ is the composite of the successive comparison for $(a,\beta)$, transport by this equality, and the inverse successive comparison for $(\alpha,a')$. These are definitions of presentation and normalization data; existence of such data is a separate assertion.
